_comment: Copy to servers.json (git-ignored) and list the downstream MCP servers you want mounted. Reference secrets by ENV NAME only — never paste values here. They load lazily, so mounting many costs almost no context. Delete any example you don't want.
_resolution: The server reads servers.json from (in order): $VIBECODERS_SERVERS → ~/.vibecoders/servers.json → ./servers.json (repo root).
_versions_note: Versions below are pinned for supply-chain hygiene. Bump them deliberately; an unpinned @latest pulls whatever is newest at spawn time.
_mounting_local_or_gui_servers: To mount a LOCAL server (a GUI-automation server like ghost-os, or any custom MCP), point command at an absolute path, e.g. { "command": "node", "args": ["/abs/path/to/server.js"], "lazy": true }. Mounting is how vibecoders reaches the desktop/device surface without bundling it.
_messages_note: The 'messages' example mounts mac_messages_mcp (iMessage/SMS) and needs `uv` (https://docs.astral.sh/uv) plus macOS Full Disk Access for your terminal. Remove it if you're not on macOS.
_lazy_note: lazy:true (the default) = the server stays cold and is spawned only on first on-demand use, costing nothing at boot. lazy:false = the server is connected and its tools indexed eagerly at startup, so a search_tools hits it instantly — set it on the one or two servers you reach for every session. Eager connects are fail-soft and bounded, so a slow lazy:false server never blocks boot.
